prompt: Customers whose credit applications are declined by a model want to know which factors led to the decision.
tells: which factors led to the decision
why: Explaining how a decision was made is transparency.
trap: Wanting an explanation is not the same as appealing to a person (accountability).

prompt: A support chat should make clear to customers that they are talking to an AI, not a person.
tells: make clear to customers that they are talking to an AI
trap: A system prompt could implement it, but the principle is transparency.

prompt: The team publishes what the model was trained on, what it's good at, and where it tends to be wrong.
tells: where it tends to be wrong
why: Documenting purpose and limitations is transparency.
trap: Publishing limits doesn't make it more reliable; it makes it understandable.

prompt: Images made by a generative model are labeled with metadata saying they were AI-generated.
tells: labeled with metadata saying they were AI-generated
why: Labeling AI-generated content tells people what they're looking at: transparency.
trap: Content filters block harmful images; labeling is about disclosure.

prompt: A team publishes a document describing the model's intended uses, training data and known failure cases.
tells: intended uses, training data and known failure cases
why: A model card or transparency note documents what a system is and isn't for.
trap: It documents the limits; it doesn't fix them.

prompt: A research assistant shows which retrieved passages each answer was based on so users can judge it themselves.
tells: so users can judge it themselves
why: Showing how an answer was produced is transparency.
trap: RAG produces the passages; showing them to users is the transparency.
